fidelity: F2a — Thevenin Equivalent-Circuit Model (1-RC/2-RC) with Solid-Electrolyte Arrhenius Resistance and Lumped Thermal ODE
description: Thevenin ECM: Coulomb-counted SOC, OCV(SOC) for a Li-metal/cathode cell, series solid-electrolyte ionic resistance R0(T) (dominant, strong Arrhenius), interfacial charge-transfer RC branches R1/C1 (+ optional R2/C2), and a lumped thermal ODE integrated with scipy.solve_ivp.
source: Janek & Zeier (2016), Nat. Energy 1, 16141; Takada (2013), Acta Materialia 61, 759-770; Murugan et al. (2007), Angew. Chem. (LLZO garnet); Kato et al. (2016), Nat. Energy 1, 16030 (Li10GeP2S12 sulfide); Plett (2015), Battery Management Systems Vol. I.

cell.name: Generic solid-state Li-metal cell (LiCoO2 cathode / sulfide-or-garnet solid electrolyte / Li metal anode)
cell.source: Janek & Zeier (2016), Nat. Energy 1, 16141; QuantumScape & Solid Power technology disclosures

capacity_ref.note: Nominal capacity at T_ref (298.15 K); reused from EC027 F1b

ocv_coefficients.description: OCV(SOC) = a0 + a1*SOC + a2*SOC^2 + a3*SOC^3 + a4*SOC^4 + a5*SOC^5 (monotonic increasing on [0,1])
ocv_coefficients.source: Polynomial fit to representative solid-state Li-metal cell discharge curve; reused verbatim from EC027 F1b

ecm.description: Series solid-electrolyte ionic resistance R0 (Arrhenius, dominant) + interfacial charge-transfer RC branches. Decomposition of the F1b lumped R_ref=0.045 Ohm into a bulk-ionic and an interfacial part.

R0_ref.note: Series solid-electrolyte ionic (bulk + grain-boundary) resistance at T_ref. Dominant term in solid-state cells; carries the high activation energy.
R0_ref.source: Janek & Zeier (2016) Nat. Energy 1,16141; Murugan et al. (2007) LLZO; Kato et al. (2016) Li10GeP2S12

E_a_R0.note: Activation energy for solid-electrolyte ionic conduction. Higher than liquid electrolytes (~15-20 kJ/mol): LLZO garnet ~30-40 kJ/mol, sulfide LGPS ~25-37 kJ/mol. Drives strong cold-temperature penalty.
E_a_R0.source: Murugan et al. (2007) Angew. Chem. 46,7778 (LLZO ~0.30 eV); Kato et al. (2016) Nat. Energy 1,16030; Takada (2013) Acta Mat. 61,759

R1_ref.note: Interfacial (charge-transfer / SE|electrode contact) resistance at T_ref, first RC branch.

E_a_R1.note: Activation energy of interfacial charge-transfer; typically even higher than bulk ionic transport (~40-60 kJ/mol).
E_a_R1.source: Takada (2013) Acta Mat. 61,759; Wenzel et al. (2016) Solid State Ionics 286,24

C1.note: First RC capacitance -> tau1 = R1*C1 ~ 96 s, slow interfacial relaxation typical of solid-state interphases.

R2_ref.note: Second (fast) RC interfacial branch at T_ref; optional, used when n_rc=2.

E_a_R2.note: Activation energy of fast interfacial branch.

C2.note: Second RC capacitance -> tau2 = R2*C2 ~ 2.4 s, fast double-layer relaxation.

n_rc.note: Number of RC branches (1 or 2). Default 2-RC Thevenin.

dOCV_dT.note: Entropic coefficient (reversible heat); reused from EC027 F1b.
dOCV_dT.source: Thomas & Newman (2003), J. Electrochem. Soc. 150(2), A176-A192

cp_cell.source: Bernardi et al. (1985) J. Electrochem. Soc. 132,5; typical Li-ion value

hA.note: Convective heat-transfer coefficient times surface area (natural convection, single cell).

temperature_K.note: -10 to 60 degC. Solid-state cells perform very poorly cold (strong R Arrhenius).
